- Peak QPS: low tens of reqs/sec; average request size ~1.2k tokens

2) Core asks we agreed to follow up on:
- Per-1M-token unit economics in US vs EU (data residency impact)
- Budget band you're targeting for pilot and 6-12 month scale
- Any procurement/security docs you need for an SOW/PO

3) Next steps (owner):
- I'll send a short pricing model with US vs EU line items and exemplar monthly cost runs (SEAN) - attached.
- Marissa will join procurement conversations and share contract timeline (MARISSA).
- Dylan can run a quick estimate of caching/batching savings given your 1.2k token average (DYLAN).

High-level guidance to set expectations: for Redwood hosted inference we typically see a regional premium for EU-hosted serving of ~10-20% due to higher infra and inter-region networking costs, plus any data-residency compliance overhead. I put together an illustrative cost table in the attached workbook.

If that matches your memory, I'll follow up with a short email tomorrow with concrete $/1M token lines and 3 rollout scenarios (pilot, steady-state, aggressive).

Thanks again -
Sean

Subject: Re: Recap + next steps - pricing & regional residency

Great questions, Alice - below are the concrete numbers and mapping. I included assumptions so your finance folks can reconcile to chargeback buckets.

Assumptions (for the attached workbook):
- Model uses Redwood hosted inference (no Dedicated)
- Average request size = 1.2k tokens; discounting possible with prefix caching and batching (see notes)
- Published baseline unit (US) = $8.50 per 1M tokens (generation + context)
- EU hosting premium = +15% on baseline (covers infra, cross-region networking & compliance ops) => EU unit = $9.78 per 1M tokens

Pilot / scale mapping (illustrative):
- Pilot band $3k/month => tokens = (budget / $ per 1M) * 1,000,000
  - Using US unit $8.50 per 1M: $3,000 -> ~352M tokens/month; $5,000 -> ~588M tokens/month
- Production band $25k/month -> ~2.94B tokens/month; $50k/month -> ~5.88B tokens/month

Important: those token counts are large - if your expected request volume was 20M-80M tokens/month then your pilot budget bands will cover much more capacity. Most customers are quoting budgets in dollars but actual token consumption varies widely by feature. Two realistic scenarios to consider for mapping budget to usage:

Scenario A (conservative consumption): average cost after batching/caching ~ $4.50 per 1M tokens (effective)
- $3k/month -> ~666M tokens/month
- $25k/month -> ~5.55B tokens/month

Scenario B (no caching, raw published unit): US baseline $8.50/1M -> $3k/month -> ~352M tokens/month

EU impact example (apply +15%):
- If effective $4.50/1M (US), EU effective = $5.18/1M; $25k/month -> ~4.82B tokens (vs 5.55B in US)
- If baseline $8.50/1M (US), EU = $9.78/1M

Notes on what drives cost differences beyond the per-1M token unit:
- Data residency: EU-only hosting requires dedicated region routing. There's no additional license fee, but we typically recommend a short-term Dedicated pool for high-volume EU-only customers to ensure predictable throughput - that can change unit economics (we can model in the workbook).
- Batching & caching: given your average request size (1.2k), we expect batching and prefix caching to reduce billable tokens by ~10-30% depending on prompt patterns. Dylan can run a sample runbook if you share a small sample of typical prompts.
- Support/SLAs: EU residency itself doesn't automatically increase support fees; however, enterprise SLAs or an on-prem Private deployment will have separate pricing lines.

Recommended next steps:
1) I'll rework the attached workbook to show the three concrete scenarios (pilot/steady/aggressive) with both US and EU lines and final $/1M rows so it maps to your chargeback numbers.
2) Marissa - can you lead procurement cadence? If Procurement confirms PO timing, we'll prepare a preliminary SOW and EU data-residency appendix.
3) Alice - if you can share a 48-72 hour sample of 200-500 anonymized prompts, Dylan will produce a caching/batching delta estimate.

I'll follow up with the revised workbook by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Sean
